verdict.rationale: Zep documents API calls an agent could invoke itself to add memory (thread.add_messages ingests into the Context Graph), search it (hybrid semantic plus BM25 graph search), and delete it (edge, node, and user deletion). A Memory MCP Server and framework integrations expose this memory to agents and MCP clients, but the evidence never lists which tools the MCP server provides or shows an explicit update operation. missing for 10: documented explicit memory update/edit operation, evidence of which add/search/update/delete tools the Memory MCP Server exposes for mid-conversation agent self-invocation, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can manage its own memory mid-conversation — adding, searching, updating, and deleting memories through tools or API calls it invokes itself

citations.quote: Chat messages are added to threads using `thread.add_messages`, which both adds those messages to the thread history and ingests those messages into the user-level knowledge graph.
Zep graph search combines semantic similarity with BM25 full-text search.
Here's how to delete an edge from a graph: client.graph.edge.delete(uuid_="your_edge_uuid")
The Memory MCP Server lets an end user connect an MCP client (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others) to their own agent memory in Zep.
Zep integrations for agent frameworks support agent memory, Context Graph search, and context placement.
